t: The graded levels: the machine, the bins and the score
html:
Part IV built one machine and one program. Part V is twenty-two puzzles, each on a machine built from the same palette parts as everything else in this book, each with a score and a par time: the graded levels. Every program printed in the chapters that follow has run to completion, every part in the right bin, before it was printed, and the program’s own regression runs them again on every release.

Opening a level

File → New Project…: the graded levels are the first section of the catalogue, as tiles in order of difficulty, each with its picture, its difficulty, its par and your best score; the Start Page’s plant floor opens them too (chapter 3). A level you have not touched opens with an empty program and its machine; one you have worked on opens where you left it, because each level keeps its own floor and program. Finishing a level records your best score and time, and My Progress keeps them all.

The bottle-sort machine

Levels 1 to 3, 5 and 6 share one machine:

  • Hopper: an Emitter in edge mode, limited to the level’s number of bottles. Infeed_Release drops one bottle on each rising edge; Infeed_Ready is 1 while the exit is clear.
  • Main_Belt: one belt the length of the floor; Conveyor_Run runs it.
  • The inspection gantry: PE_Inspect (a bottle is here), three retro beams at 30, 44 and 52 px (PE_Low, PE_Mid, PE_High: a small bottle is 40 px tall and breaks only the low one, a medium is 48 and breaks two, a large is 56 and breaks all three), the colour sensor’s three banks (Color_Red, Color_Blue, Color_Green) and the crack eye (Crack_Sensor, broken bottles only).
  • The filler: a dispenser over the belt (Fill_Valve), the fill-level sensor beside the nozzle with its analog percent (Fill_Level, 0–100 % of the bottle’s own label) and the presence eye under the nozzle (PE_Fill).
  • One pusher and one bin per lane: Div1 … Div6 extend the pushers; each pusher has its own eye, PE_Div1 …, just ahead of the arm.
  • The end of the line: PE_LineEnd and a remover that takes anything nobody pushed.
  • The console: Start_PB, Stop_PB (a plain button on this machine), E_Stop (1 while healthy), Lamp_Run, Lamp_Fault.

Every name in the list is an alias tag the level makes for you, pointing at the part’s I/O point:

The later levels bring their own machines: Level 10 ends the belt in the case packer and VFD lane of the bottle line’s step 12; Level 11 and Level 21 are the mix tank and its kitchen; Levels 4, 7, 8, 12, 14 and 15 are a finished-bottle line with a camera, a laser marker, a labeler or a reject station; Level 13 is the servo axis; Level 22 is a paint line and Level 20 its bulk filler; Level 16 a checkweigher; Levels 17 and 18 a line of machine blocks; Levels 9 and 19 no machine at all, only a camera on a socket. Each chapter describes its machine and lists its tags.

Graded bins and the score

Each bin carries a Grading rule (whole or broken bottles, a size, a colour, must be filled) set in its Properties, and it scores what lands in it: +100 for the right part, −50 for the wrong one, −40 for the right bin with a wrong fill. A part that falls off the line is −50. The later levels add their own rules, each in its brief. When the hopper is empty and the belt is clear, the level completes: +200 if you are under par, and a card with your score and stars: three for no mistakes under par, two for no mistakes, one for 70 % right. Specs on the simulator toolbar shows each bin’s rule. The level’s brief sits under the simulator, and Help → Level Brief and Scoring has it in full.

Guided mode on a level

A level opens with the guided-mode panel on, following that level’s chapter: the tags to make, every rung of the chapter’s program under its fold (hints first, chapter 15), a check that MainRoutine verifies, and the results it ticks while you run the level, among them complete, every part right, under par. Next level on the score card builds the next level and keeps the panel on.

Each chapter is built like the lessons of Part IV: what the level asks, the tags, every rung as the editor draws it with the text you type, what the rungs do, Run it, and the traps. Write each program into MainRoutine. File → Start Level N Over… puts the level back the way it first opens; tick Keep my I/O configuration to keep a camera module’s address and connection.
